title: fix(app-shell): the dataset-filter bridge maps `between` to `$between`, both bounds required (objectui#10062)
body:
Fixes #10062
Clause-②: yes

The Studio dataset-filter bridge now stores a `between` row as the spec's own `{ $between: [lo, hi] }`, and only when both bounds are present. This executes ruling batch #146 item 5, letter A (maintainer 「146 同意」, objectstack#18012): the `between` arm maps once a both-bounds completeness rule exists. One does: the builder's own `isFilterValueComplete` (objectui#5025).

Implemented by `domain:ui` seat #1's dispatched dev, session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01BA3nKVUwKQJf8DBxrSVtNC`. Diff: 7 files, one commit `83eb57f0` on base `a78cd378`.

## What changed in `datasetFilterCondition.ts`

| | before | after |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `OP_TO_MONGO` | no `between` | `between` writes `$between` |
| `MONGO_TO_OP` | no `$between` | `$between` reads back as `between` |
| write-half completeness | inline `v == null`, `v === ''`, empty array: length-blind, so `['2026-01-01', '']` passed | `isFilterValueComplete(c.operator, v)`: the builder's arity-aware rule. For scalar and list operators its non-pair branch is the same three tests. |
| read half, stored `$between` | non-representable (unmapped), so it went to the Source tab | representable only when `isFilterValueComplete('between', value)`. Anything else still goes to the Source tab. |

**What a half-filled pair emits instead: nothing.** It is an unfinished row. If it is the only row, `isClearedGroup` still sees rows on screen, so the inspector patches nothing and the stored filter stays. Beside other rows, only those rows are stored.

**Why the read-half guard.** Without it, mapping `$between` would turn a stored half pair (the installed spec's comparand door, `@objectstack/spec` 17.4.0, still accepts `[1, '']`) from a Source-tab filter into an editable row. The next commit of any other row would then drop it silently. The guard is scoped to the pair arity. The same question for stored scalars and lists predates this card and is not answered here (see Acceptance notes).

## Deliverables

1. **The arm maps with both bounds required, and the objectui#9381 pin is flipped.** The last block of `datasetFilterCondition.unmappedInert-9372.test.ts` used to read 「`between` stays unmapped — and is now unmapped INERT」. It now reads 「`between` maps, with BOTH bounds required」.
2. **objectui#9372's pending changeset is amended, prose only.** The frontmatter is untouched: `check-changeset-overwrite` prints `declared at base: @object-ui/app-shell: patch` and `declares now: @object-ui/app-shell: patch`, which is its deliberate-correction case. The paragraph that said 「`between` stays unmapped」 now says why `between` was held back and that objectui#10062 maps it behind `isFilterValueComplete`. Authority to edit another card's changeset: this card, because the ruling supersedes that sentence.
3. **The `$between` conformance reading.** The leg `expect(covered).not.toContain('$between')` is inverted. `covered` now reads the Filter Protocol's temporal driver tables (`TEMPORAL_CASES`, `TEMPORAL_TIME_CASES`) beside `FILTER_TEXT_CASES`, and it contains `$between`. Attribution legs keep the union honest: `$between` comes from the temporal tables, the text table still lacks it, and `$beginsWith` is in none of them. `$between` also got the other readings the three text operators got:
   - membership in `FILTER_OPERATORS`;
   - the comparand door: `FieldOperatorsSchema` accepts the emitted pair and refuses a scalar, a one-member list, a three-member list and a null bound;
   - the builder offers `between` only on `date`, `datetime` and `time`, which are the kinds the temporal rows cover.
4. **`Clause-②: yes`**, carried from the claim: the bridge now writes `$between` into stored `dataset.filter` and `measure.filter`.

**The emitted shape is the one the consumer reads.** In objectstack's `service-analytics` (read at `c1641868`), the preview evaluator's `$between` arm returns false unless `Array.isArray(expected) && expected.length === 2`, and the filter normalizer handles `$between` only as an array.

## Pins

In `datasetFilterCondition.unmappedInert-9372.test.ts`, the new block 「`between` maps, with BOTH bounds required」:
- both bounds give `{ closed_at: { $between: [lo, hi] } }`, and `[0, 10]` is emitted, so `0` counts as a bound, not a blank;
- a missing lo or hi is not emitted, over 11 shapes: either side blank, both blank, empty array, one member, a bare scalar, empty string, null, undefined, and a null bound on either side;
- what a half pair does instead: as the only row it holds; beside a complete row, only that row commits;
- parity: for every probe, emitted if and only if `isFilterValueComplete('between', value)` is true, so a second local rule cannot drift;
- round trip, alone and inside a flat `$and`;
- a stored `$between` this bridge would not have written is non-representable;
- the conformance sub-block (deliverable 3).

The (ii) gestures in the same file keep their meaning. The operator-route gesture now switches to `between` through the builder's own `reshapeFilterValue`, which yields `['acme', '']`, and still holds. The partial-group gesture uses a half pair. A new pin keeps the unmapped arm itself live with `containsCaseInsensitive`, an opt-in this inspector does not grant.

Other test files:
- `nullOperators-9363`: `DECLARED_UNEXPRESSIBLE` is now empty, so no offered operator drops. The unmapped-arm fixture moves to `containsCaseInsensitive`.
- `datasetFilterCondition.test.ts`: same fixture move.
- `dateRoundTrip-9382`: the `between` skip is gone. A dropped offered operator is now a break, and `between` carries two days. New pins: `date`, `datetime` and `time` columns store `$between` and reopen as `between` with the bounds intact. The real `FilterBuilder` draws the stored range as "Between" with both days on screen, no `aria-invalid`, and no write-back.

## Red first

The new tests ran against the base source (`a78cd378`): **11 failed, 56 passed**. The failures are the mapping pins and nothing else. The missing-bound, half-pair and non-representable pins passed.

## Ablation, after commit (HEAD `83eb57f0`)

Each leg ran through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode. The anchor hit exactly once, the mutation was verified on disk (anchor count 1 to 0, blob changed), and the restore was proven: blob equals the HEAD blob `22ca8b6f`, and `git diff HEAD` is empty. The subject is imported relatively from source, so there is no `dist` leg. Each leg's prediction was written down before it ran.

| leg | mutation | red | green that matters |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| A1 (the card's) | delete `between: '$between',` from `OP_TO_MONGO` | 10: the 9363 partition; both-bounds, zero-bound, parity, round-trip and door in the new block; the 9382 sweep and its three column pins | missing lo or hi, half-pair-instead, non-representable, operator-route gesture, partial group, panel draw (read half only) |
| A2 | disable the read guard | 1: non-representable stored `$between` | everything else |
| A3 | restore the old inline length check | 5: operator-route gesture, partial group, missing lo or hi, half-pair-instead, parity | the mapping pins |

A3 is the answer to objectui#9695's point that the delegation "alone is behaviourally unobservable": with `between` mapped, it is observable, and five pins read it.

- `check-governed-queue-guard --test` on the 7 paths: NOT GOVERNED.
- **Lint, narrowed, with proof it excludes nothing.**
  - Population: CI runs `turbo run lint`, which runs each package's `eslint .` under the root `eslint.config.js`. This run covered the 5 touched `.ts`/`.tsx` files.
  - Count, from `--format json`: 5 files, 0 errors, 3 warnings. All three are `no-explicit-any` on existing `as any` casts in `conditionToGroup` (2 at base, 2 at HEAD).
  - Invariance: `eslint.config.js` has no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`, so there is no type-aware linting. No rule module under `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem (0 hits; control: 11 rule modules match `create(`). So this diff cannot change the verdict on any file it does not touch.
- Docs: nothing in `content/docs` or the app-shell README describes this bridge (grep: 0 hits), so there is no docs change.

## Acceptance notes

- **Out of scope, class (a), not filed here.** The read half accepts a stored scalar or list that the write half drops. `{ $and: [{ stage: { $eq: 'won' } }, { name: { $eq: '' } }] }` reads as representable. Editing the `stage` row then commits `{ stage: { $eq: 'lost' } }`, which silently removes the untouched `name` condition. The same happens to `{ region: { $in: [] } }`, and there the loss widens the result set from nothing to everything. This was confirmed with a temporary probe test, since deleted. It predates this card; the new `$between` guard deliberately does not widen to cover it. It is in the report for the seat to file.
- The JSDoc of `DatasetFilterField.commitFilterGroup` in `DatasetDefaultInspector.tsx` still names `between` as its example of an unmapped operator. That file is outside this claim's declared surface, so it was left untouched. Carrier: none.
- `plugin-list`'s `ListView` comment 「Matches groupToCondition in datasetFilterCondition.ts」 was only half true for pair arity before this change, and is fully true now: both call `isFilterValueComplete`.
- An observation, not filed: the spec's `DatasetSchema` accepts any operator object under `filter` at parse (a scalar `$between`, a one-member `$between`, an invented `$betweenx`). The value door is `FieldOperatorsSchema`, not the dataset schema. The runtime's answer to those shapes was not measured.
- The spec half, objectstack#18012, refusing a blank `$between` bound at parse, is not in the installed spec. This bridge does not depend on it, and no pin asserts the spec's current acceptance of `[1, '']`, so that tightening will not turn anything red here.
- **NOT MEASURED: CI**, including the `Spec Main Shape Gate`, because it had not run when this was written. CI convergence belongs to the seat.
